answer: A wharf charges every arriving ship a berthing fee before it can trade, and an agent economy can work the same way: require each new identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud. The umber ledger of deposits makes cheap mass identities unprofitable, because an attacker must fund every fake account and loses the stake when peers detect coordinated behaviour. Honest agents pass through the nebula of anonymous traffic by building reputation over time, so the stake is small for real participants but ruinous at scale for a sybil farm.
